entry.title: GHSA-F8H5-X737-X4XR: Finch-Rust: The Shai-Hulud Worm Burrows into Crates.io
entry.summary:
Finch-Rust: The Shai-Hulud Worm Burrows into Crates.io
Vulnerability ID: GHSA-F8H5-X737-X4XR CVSS Score: 10.0 Published: 2026-02-06 In the ongoing saga of supply chain warfare, the Rust ecosystem—often lauded for its memory safety—has been reminded that the borrow checker cannot save you from social engineering. The 'finch-rust' crate, a malicious package mimicking a legitimate library, was found acting as a loader for the 'Shai-Hulud' malware campaign. Designed to execute arbitrary code during the build process via 'build.rs', this package serves as a stark reminder that 'cargo build' is effectively remote code execution. A malicious Rust crate named 'finch-rust' was published to crates.io, executing a malware loader during compilation. Part of the 'Shai-Hulud' campaign, it steals developer secrets (AWS, SSH, Env Vars) immediately upon running 'cargo build'. Attack Vector: Supply Chain / Typosquatting CVSS: 10.0 (Critical) Impact: Data Exfiltration / Arbitrary Code Execution Component: build.rs (Cargo Build Script) Campaign: Shai-Hulud 2.0 Status: Malware / Active Exploitation Rust Development Environments CI/CD Pipelines Linux Workstations macOS Workstations Windows Workstations finch-rust: All Versions (Fixed in: N/A (Removed)) Supply Chain Analysis: Malicious build.rs script execution upon package installation. Dependency Verification Credential Rotation Network Monitoring CI/CD Isolation Remediation Steps: Identify projects containing 'finch-rust' in Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock. Remove the dependency immediately: 'cargo remove finch-rust'. Revoke and rotate ALL credentials (AWS, SSH, GPG, API Keys) present on the infected system. Inspect ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and other persistence locations for backdoors. Rebuild the host system if possible, or perform a deep forensic audit. entry.title: COLLEGE STUDENT ENTERING THE WORLD OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
entry.summary: I am starting my journey in the world of information technology. Currently, I am pursuing an associate's degree in computer information systems, but I plan to specialize in AI and machine learning or in database administration. Right now, the biggest challenge is securing an internship, which I need to graduate. Many internship posts I see require candidates to already have one year of experience. Call me old-fashioned, but internships were designed to be where you gain experience so that after a year, you can start applying for entry-level positions. In fact, a fellow college student I shared a class with said he saw an engineering internship that required five years of experience to qualify. This paradox makes breaking into the field incredibly difficult for students like me. I am partnering with my career services department to revamp my resume as I continue my education. My resume now highlights my projects, clubs, and experience as a customer service representative. Despite these challenges, I remain optimistic about finding an opportunity that values potential and eagerness to learn.
